proposals.before: King Chen accordingly appointed his old friend wuchen, a native of Chen, as general, with Shao Sao as protector of the army and Zhang Er and Chen Yu as colonels of the left and right. He gave them three thousand soldiers and sent them north to conquer the land of Zhao.
proposals.after: King Chen accordingly appointed his old friend Wu Chen, a native of Chen, as general, with Shao Sao as protector of the army and Zhang Er and Chen Yu as colonels of the left and right. He gave them three thousand soldiers and sent them north to conquer the land of Zhao.
proposals.reason: The personal name 武臣 is left uncapitalized as “wuchen” instead of the standard romanization “Wu Chen”.

proposals.before: wuchen and his officers crossed the Yellow River at Baima and visited the counties along their route, rallying the local leaders with these words: 'For decades, Qin has tyrannized the realm with misrule and savage punishments.
proposals.after: Wu Chen and his officers crossed the Yellow River at Baima and visited the counties along their route, rallying the local leaders with these words: 'For decades, Qin has tyrannized the realm with misrule and savage punishments.
proposals.reason: The personal name 武臣 is left uncapitalized as “wuchen” instead of the standard romanization “Wu Chen”.

proposals.before: They marched on, rallying troops as they went, and gathered tens of thousands of men. wuchen was given the title Lord of Wuxin.
proposals.after: They marched on, rallying troops as they went, and gathered tens of thousands of men. Wu Chen was given the title Lord of Wuxin.
proposals.reason: The personal name 武臣 is left uncapitalized as “wuchen” instead of the standard romanization “Wu Chen”.

proposals.before: They then spoke to wuchen: 'King Chen rose in revolt at Qi and proclaimed himself king at Chen without bothering to restore the heirs of the six states.
proposals.after: They then spoke to Wu Chen: 'King Chen rose in revolt at Qi and proclaimed himself king at Chen without bothering to restore the heirs of the six states.
proposals.reason: The personal name 武臣 is rendered as uncapitalized wuchen instead of Wu Chen.

proposals.before: They then persuaded wuchen, saying: 'King Chen rose at Qi, arrived at Chen and made himself king, without necessarily restoring the descendants of the six states.
proposals.after: They then persuaded Wu Chen, saying: 'King Chen rose at Qi, arrived at Chen and made himself king, without necessarily restoring the descendants of the six states.
proposals.reason: The personal name 武臣 is rendered as uncapitalized wuchen instead of Wu Chen.

proposals.before: Better to establish one of your brothers as king;
proposals.after: Better to establish one of his brothers as king;
proposals.reason: Chinese 立其兄弟 uses 其 after the discussion of King Chen; the idiomatic your brothers likely reverses the source referent.

proposals.before: wuchen heeded their counsel and proclaimed himself King of Zhao.
proposals.after: Wu Chen heeded their counsel and proclaimed himself King of Zhao.
proposals.reason: The personal name 武臣 is rendered as uncapitalized wuchen instead of Wu Chen.

proposals.before: wuchen then heeded their advice and thereupon established himself as King of Zhao.
proposals.after: Wu Chen then heeded their advice and thereupon established himself as King of Zhao.
proposals.reason: The personal name 武臣 is rendered as uncapitalized wuchen instead of Wu Chen.

proposals.before: When word reached King Chen, he was furious. He wanted to exterminate the families of wuchen and the others and send an army to attack Zhao.
proposals.after: When word reached King Chen, he was furious. He wanted to exterminate the families of Wu Chen and the others and send an army to attack Zhao.
proposals.reason: The personal name 武臣 is rendered as uncapitalized wuchen instead of Wu Chen.

proposals.before: They sent someone to report to King Chen. King Chen was furious and wished to exterminate the clans of wuchen and the others and to send troops to attack Zhao.
proposals.after: They sent someone to report to King Chen. King Chen was furious and wished to exterminate the clans of Wu Chen and the others and to send troops to attack Zhao.
proposals.reason: The personal name 武臣 is rendered as uncapitalized wuchen instead of Wu Chen.

proposals.before: His chancellor, Lord Fang, remonstrated: 'Qin has not yet fallen. If you execute the families of wuchen and his companions, you will only create another Qin.
proposals.after: His chancellor, Lord Fang, remonstrated: 'Qin has not yet fallen. If you execute the families of Wu Chen and his companions, you will only create another Qin.
proposals.reason: The personal name 武臣 is rendered as uncapitalized wuchen instead of Wu Chen.

proposals.before: King Chen's Chancellor, Lord Fang, remonstrated, saying: 'Qin has not yet fallen, and if you execute the families of wuchen and the others, you will merely create another Qin.
proposals.after: King Chen's Chancellor, Lord Fang, remonstrated, saying: 'Qin has not yet fallen, and if you execute the families of Wu Chen and the others, you will merely create another Qin.
proposals.reason: The personal name 武臣 is rendered as uncapitalized wuchen instead of Wu Chen.

proposals.before: King Chen agreed and adopted this plan. He moved the families of wuchen and the others into the palace as hostages and enfeoffed Zhang Er's son Zhang Ao as Lord of Chengdu.
proposals.after: King Chen agreed and adopted this plan. He moved the families of Wu Chen and the others into the palace as hostages and enfeoffed Zhang Er's son Zhang Ao as Lord of Chengdu.
proposals.reason: The personal name 武臣 is rendered as uncapitalized wuchen instead of Wu Chen.

proposals.before: King Chen agreed, followed his plan, moved the families of wuchen and the others into the palace under house arrest, and enfeoffed Zhang Er's son Ao as Lord of Chengdu.
proposals.after: King Chen agreed, followed his plan, moved the families of Wu Chen and the others into the palace under house arrest, and enfeoffed Zhang Er's son Ao as Lord of Chengdu.
proposals.reason: The personal name 武臣 is rendered as uncapitalized wuchen instead of Wu Chen.

proposals.before: Zhang Er and Chen Yu counseled wuchen: 'Your kingship over Zhao was never Chu's true desire. They congratulated you only as a matter of strategy.
proposals.after: Zhang Er and Chen Yu counseled Wu Chen: 'Your kingship over Zhao was never Chu's true desire. They congratulated you only as a matter of strategy.
proposals.reason: The personal name 武臣 is rendered as uncapitalized wuchen instead of Wu Chen.

proposals.before: Zhang Er and Chen Yu persuaded wuchen, saying: 'Your becoming King of Zhao was not Chu's true wish; they merely congratulated you as a stratagem.
proposals.after: Zhang Er and Chen Yu persuaded Wu Chen, saying: 'Your becoming King of Zhao was not Chu's true wish; they merely congratulated you as a stratagem.
proposals.reason: The personal name 武臣 is rendered as uncapitalized wuchen instead of Wu Chen.

proposals.before: wuchen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu conquered dozens of cities in Zhao with nothing but riding crops. Each of them wants to face south and rule as king. Do you really think they are content to remain ministers forever?
proposals.after: Wu Chen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu conquered dozens of cities in Zhao with nothing but riding crops. Each of them wants to face south and rule as king. Do you really think they are content to remain ministers forever?
proposals.reason: The personal name 武臣 is rendered as uncapitalized wuchen instead of Wu Chen.

proposals.before: wuchen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu wielded riding crops and took dozens of Zhao cities; each of them wants to face south and rule as king—do you think they wish to remain ministers to the end of their days?
proposals.after: Wu Chen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu wielded riding crops and took dozens of Zhao cities; each of them wants to face south and rule as king—do you think they wish to remain ministers to the end of their days?
proposals.reason: The personal name 武臣 is rendered as uncapitalized wuchen instead of Wu Chen.

proposals.before: How can a minister be compared to a sovereign? It is simply that the situation was not yet settled, and they did not dare divide the territory among themselves. So they set up wuchen as king first, by seniority, to hold the loyalty of Zhao.
proposals.after: How can a minister be compared to a sovereign? It is simply that the situation was not yet settled, and they did not dare divide the territory among themselves. So they set up Wu Chen as king first, by seniority, to hold the loyalty of Zhao.
proposals.reason: The personal name 武臣 is rendered as uncapitalized wuchen instead of Wu Chen.

proposals.before: How can minister and master be spoken of in the same breath? It is only that the situation has just been settled and they did not dare divide the land and make themselves kings; so for now, by seniority, they first established wuchen as king to hold the hearts of Zhao.
proposals.after: How can minister and master be spoken of in the same breath? It is only that the situation has just been settled and they did not dare divide the land and make themselves kings; so for now, by seniority, they first established Wu Chen as king to hold the hearts of Zhao.
proposals.reason: The personal name 武臣 is rendered as uncapitalized wuchen instead of Wu Chen.

proposals.before: The king's sister was drunk and did not recognize him as a general. She sent a rider to dismiss him with a casual wave.
proposals.after: The king's sister was drunk and did not recognize him as a general. She sent a rider to dismiss him.
proposals.reason: Chinese 使騎謝李良 says she sent a rider to decline or dismiss Li Liang; 'with a casual wave' is not in the source.

proposals.before: Handan was caught completely off guard, and wuchen and Shao Sao were both killed.
proposals.after: Handan was caught completely off guard, and Wu Chen and Shao Sao were both killed.
proposals.reason: 武臣 is the personal name Wu Chen; the lowercase 'wuchen' fails to mark it as a person name.

proposals.before: Handan was caught unawares, and in the end wuchen and Shao Sao were killed.
proposals.after: Handan was caught unawares, and in the end Wu Chen and Shao Sao were killed.
proposals.reason: The same personal name 武臣 is left as uncapitalized 'wuchen' in the literal English.

proposals.before: Zhang Er was routed and fled. Considering which lord might take him in, he said, 'The King of Han and I are old friends. Xiang Yu is powerful, and it was he who made me king, but I wish to go to Chu.'
proposals.after: Zhang Er was routed and fled. Considering that there was no lord he could turn to, he said, 'The King of Han and I are old friends. Xiang Yu is powerful, and it was he who made me king, but I wish to go to Chu.'
proposals.reason: The Chinese 念諸侯無可歸者 states that Zhang Er judged no feudal lord a viable refuge, not that he was weighing which lord might receive him.

proposals.before: The King of Zhao was young, and the state had only recently been restored, so Chen Yu did not depart for his own kingdom. Instead, he remained to serve as the king's tutor, while sending Xia Yue to govern Dai as chancellor.
proposals.after: The King of Zhao was weak, and the state had only recently been restored, so Chen Yu did not depart for his own kingdom. Instead, he remained to serve as the king's tutor, while sending Xia Yue to govern Dai as chancellor.
proposals.reason: 弱 means weak, not young; the literal field already translates it correctly, and the idiomatic rendering invents youth.

proposals.before: Emperor Gaozu's eldest daughter, Princess Luyuan of Lu, became Queen of Zhao.
proposals.after: Emperor Gaozu's eldest daughter, Princess Yuan of Lu, became Queen of Zhao.
proposals.reason: 魯元公主 names the princess titled Yuan and enfeoffed in Lu; Princess Luyuan of Lu doubles the fief already expressed by 魯.

proposals.before: Through the reigns of Emperor Hui, Empress Dowager Gao, Emperor Wen, and Emperor Jing, the descendants of King Zhang's retainers all attained high office.
proposals.after: Through the reigns of Emperor Hui, Empress Dowager Gao, Emperor Wen, and Emperor Jing, the descendants of King Zhang's retainers all attained the rank of two-thousand-bushel officials.
proposals.reason: The Chinese specifies the two-thousand-bushel (二千石) rank; the idiomatic rendering flattens this to generic high office.

proposals.before: The Grand Historian remarks: Zhang Er and Chen Yu were celebrated by their contemporaries as men of extraordinary virtue.
proposals.after: The Grand Historian remarks: Zhang Er and Chen Yu were called worthy men in the traditions handed down through the ages.
proposals.reason: 世傳 marks transmitted tradition across generations, not celebration by contemporaries.
